# Appoint or replace directors and officers

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When the company needs a new board member, officer or replacement for a departing appointee. Documented appointment or departure, required register changes and a completed authority handover.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Collect the governing documents and proposed change

agent-runnable


Gather the current board and officer registers, governing documents, investor rights and the proposed role. Identify the vacancy, effective date and responsibilities without assuming the founder can appoint unilaterally.

- Sources: [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Confirm eligibility, conflicts and the approval route

human · human approval required


Company counsel checks eligibility, nomination rights, consent requirements and any relevant local filings. Record disclosed interests and distinguish appointment authority from authority to sign contracts or access bank accounts.

- Sources: [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the appointment and handover pack

agent-runnable


Draft the resolutions, consents, role description and register changes for counsel review. List access, insurance, induction and delegated authorities that need separate changes.

- Sources: [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Obtain the required consents and authorize the change

human · human approval required


The appropriate people review and execute the approved documents. Keep the appointment pending until the required approvals and acceptance are evidenced; counsel coordinates any filings.

- Sources: [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile registers and authority changes

agent-runnable


Record the effective change, update approved private registers and verify access and signing mandates with their owners. Retain submission receipts and assign follow-up for any registry decision still pending.

- Verify: Documented appointment or departure, required register changes and a completed authority handover.
- Sources: [GOV.UK running a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/running-a-limited-company)
